Judgment

Wife, children of Narasappa filed petition under Section 166 of Imv Act claiming compensation
from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530
asserting t

hat on 15.08.2023 at 11.30 p.m. when Narasappa riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-W-1475 from Padhyapeeta towards Maruthinagar, near Divine Gym, Maruthi Nagara main road, Chandan/respondent No.2- rider of another Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530 rode the same negligently from Maruthinagara towards KLE College, dashed the same to motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-W-1475, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Narasappa.
2. As on the date of accident Narasappa being aged 51 years, used to earn Rs.1,01,268/p.m. by working as Lecturer at PU-board, Kengeri, used to contribute the entire income to the family.
3. Regarding accident Kengeri traffic police registered a case in crime No.279/2023 against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530.

4. In response to the notice, respondent No.1- insurance company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident , age occupation ,income of the deceased Narasappa.
5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2- owner of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530 appeared through his advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 24.09.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 15.08.2023 at about 11.30 p.m. on Maruthinagar main road, near Divine Gym/Padmapeeta road, in view of the negligent use of the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-W- 1475 accident taken place resulting in the death of Narasappa S/o Doddahanumanthaiah ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation ? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

9. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...

Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.90,03,588/- with current and future interest at 6%p.a. as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence PW1 stated that on 15.08.2023 at 11.30 p.m. when Narasappa riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-W-1475 from Padhyapeeta towards Maruthinagar, near Divine Gym,
Maruthi Nagara main road, Chandan/respondent No.2- rider of another Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530 rode the same negligently from Maruthinagara towards KLE College, dashed the same to motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-W-1475, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Narasappa.
11. In the written statement respondent No.1- insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident .
12. In the cross-examination, PW1 stated that she never witnessed the accident.

13. In the evidence affidavit PW2- Hanumanthegowda stated that on 15.08.2023 at about 11.30 p.m.
when he was standing in front of his house near Divine Gym, SMV layout, Kengeri, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA- 02-KF-9530 by keep sitting a person on the pillion, rode the same in high speed from Maruthinagar side towards KLE College, dashed the same to two wheeler bearing No.KA-06-W-1475 which was running from Padmapeeta road towards Maruthinagara main road,
thereby caused accident, made riders of both the vehicles and pillion to fell on the road and dragged the rider of two wheeler bearing No.KA-06-W-1475 for a distance of 50 to 60 feet, resulting in the head injuries and instantaneous death.
PW.2 stated that immediately after the accident pillion rider of the motorcycle No.KA-02-KF-9530 and rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-06-W-1475 have been shifted to the hospital.
14. In the cross-examination PW.2 stated that he witnessed the accident and on the date of the accident police have recorded his statement.
In the cross- examination PW.2 denied the suggestion about non- witnessing the accident.

17. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequences of the accident.
In this case evidence of the respondent No.2-owner/rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-02-KF-9530 is not available.

Hence, I have concluded that on 15.08.2023 at 11.30 p.m. when Narasappa was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-W- 1475 from Padhyapeeta towards Maruthinagar, near Divine Gym, Maruthi Nagara main road, Chandan/respondent No.2- rider of another Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF- 9530 rode the same negligently from Maruthinagara towards KLE College, dashed the same to motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-W-1475, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Narasappa.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

In the evidence PW1 stated that as on the date of accident her husband deceased Narasappa being aged about 51 years, used to earn Rs.1,01,268/p.m. by working as Lecturer at Kengeri PU college and used to contribute entire income to the family.
19. In the written statement respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of the deceased.

20. In the cross-examination PW1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident she never dependend on her husband Narasappa and as on the date of accident her husband never earning Rs.1,01,268/- per month.
21. In the evidence PW.2- Hanumanthegowda and RW.1 - officer of the insurance company stated nothing regarding the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
22. In the PM report/inquest mahazar age of the deceased noted as 52 years.

In the copy of Aadhaar card and DL marked at Ex.P.7 and P.16 the date of birth of Narasappa is noted as 01.06.1972.
23.

28. Issue No.3: In the written statement respondent No.1-insurance company and in the evidence affidavit

RW.1-officer of the insurance company submitted that as on the date of accident Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF- 9530 had insurance coverage, however denied the liability to indemnify the respondent No.2- Chandan/owner and rider of the motorcycle on the ground that as on the date of accident Chandan had no licence to ride the motorcycle with gear, thereby violated the driver clause of the policy.
In the evidence RW1 produced the copy of the notice under Sec.133 of MV Act issued by the police and reply to that notice by the respondent No.1 to the police at Ex.R.2 and 3.

In the cross-examination RW1 denied suggestion that respondent No.1-insurance company is bound to pay compensation to the petitioners and as on the date of the incident respondent No.2- Chandan had licence to ride motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530.
30.

As referred above after investigation police have filed charge sheet against respondent No.2- Chandhan S/o Veerachar owner and rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 02-KF-9530 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.3(1), 181 of MV Act.
In the reply dated 12.03.2024 submitted by Chandan to IO marked at Ex.R.3 Chandan has not mentioned identification number of the driving licence possessed by him as on the date of incident.
Hence, it is clear as on the date of incident Chandan had no licence to ride motorcycle with gear and by riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530 has violated driver clause of the policy.

31. On 03.03.2025 learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted xerox copy of the judgment dated 31.01.2025 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad in First Appeal No.1780/2024 C/w 1776/2024 & 1777/2024 between ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.
Ltd.,V/s Smt. Arti Devi & others requested to pass order directing respondent No.1- insurance company to pay compensation amount then recover the same from the respondent No.2.

sentences.text: In the judgment cited on behalf of the petitioner the driver and owner of the vehicle which caused the accident are different.
In this case owner and rider of the motorcycle namely Chandan are one and the same.
Hence the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Alhabad cited on behalf of the petitioners is not applicable to the facts and circumstances of this case.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondent No.2 who violated the driver clause of the policy is not entitle to be indemnified by the respondent No.1 and Respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence,
I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.2 shall pay Rs.90,03,588/-
(Rupees ninety lakhs three thousand five hundred eighty eight only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the owner/rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-9530 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 4 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally .
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners No.1 may be released by crediting the same to her bank account directly.

Entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners No.2 and petitioner No.3 (minors) shall be deposited in any bank in their names till they attain Honnadevi S L vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164361186/
